proof:
# An exact small-budget residual-root depletion bound
turning a root-moment bound into a false volume-moment bound. It is
conditional on the cap budget being smaller than every row destination
fiber volume; it supplies no unrestricted OC inequality.

## 1. Actual section statement

Let C be an actual convex fiber family with intrinsic measured dimension
q>=1. Let distinct positive integer bases z_1,...,z_N carry positive
weights theta_j with sum theta_j=1, and suppose their barycenter p is
also an actual integer base whose section has dimension q. Write

    V_j=H_q(C_(z_j)),       v_j=V_j^(1/q).

Let H be one original closed ambient halfspace. Let B be an upper bound
on its total measured mass, and assume

    0<B<min_j V_j.                                     (1)

If u is the residual root at the source,

    u=H_q(C_p intersect H^c)^(1/q),

then

    sum_j theta_j v_j-u
      <=max_j theta_j [v_j-(V_j-B)^(1/q)].              (2)

This is valid for arbitrary oblique H. No affine centroid condition is
assumed. In a positive KKT row whose active source residual has root h_p,
one can set u=h_p and use its exact normalized row weights.

## 2. Geometric and scalar proof

Set A_j=H_q(C_(z_j) intersect H). The destination fibers are disjoint
parts of the original mixed measure, so

    A_j>=0,       sum_j A_j<=B.

By (1), every actual residual section C_(z_j) intersect H^c has positive
q-volume. The weighted Minkowski combination of these residuals is
contained in the actual residual at p: strict inequalities for H^c
are preserved by a positive convex combination. If their direction
spaces differed, that combination would have dimension greater than q,
contradicting the dimension of the actual section at p. Thus ordinary
intrinsic Brunn--Minkowski, applied to their closures if necessary, gives

    u>=sum_j theta_j (V_j-A_j)^(1/q).                   (3)

Nonclosed residuals have the same positive q-volume as their compact
convex closures. No empty residual is inserted into (3).

For 0<=s<=B define

    F_j(s)=theta_j [v_j-(V_j-s)^(1/q)].

Each F_j is convex, nonnegative and increasing, and F_j(0)=0. This is
immediate from concavity of the positive qth root; for q=1 it is a
linear function. Hence

    F_j(A_j)<= (A_j/B) F_j(B).

Summing and using sum A_j<=B proves

    sum_j F_j(A_j)<=max_j F_j(B).

Subtracting (3) from sum theta_j v_j proves (2). Equivalently, the
maximum root depletion over the relaxed simplex of cap allocations
{A>=0:sum A<=B} is attained by spending all B on one destination.
That scalar optimum is exact. No claim is made that every scalar
optimizer is realizable by one geometric cap in a fixed body.

## 3. An inverted form and its limits

If delta=sum theta_j v_j-u>0, then there is some index j with
delta<theta_j v_j and

    B>=V_j-[v_j-delta/theta_j]^q.                       (4)

Thus B is at least the minimum of the right side over eligible indices.
If there is no eligible index, no cap satisfying (1) can realize this
source residual. The strict eligibility follows from B<V_j, which
makes every remaining root positive. Formula (4) is only an equivalent
necessary test under the same small-budget hypothesis.

For equal destination volumes V and equal row weights 1/N, (2) becomes

    V^(1/q)-u <= [V^(1/q)-(V-B)^(1/q)]/N.

The bound can be vacuous when the source residual root exceeds the
row-average original volume root. It also does not handle destinations
of volume at most B: a cap can then contain a whole destination fiber,
and the residual BM step must be replaced, not continued through an
empty set. These are explicit limitations, not unproved cleanup steps.

The exact KKT/projective counterexample in
`candidate 374134af8a3f1b92`
does not contradict this bound: its selected cap's total mass exceeds
each destination fiber volume. The present estimate is a genuinely
different conditional use of the actual cap budget, but does not by
itself convert the dual loads into the lattice parity budget.
